title: Manifest entry
description: A pointer to bytes. Datasets reference their files ONLY through manifest entries, never through a filename written into code. Exactly one location form is allowed per entry -- path, url, lfs_oid, or uri -- so a set that outgrows a git repo is relocated by editing one field, with the checksum proving the bytes did not change.

path.description: Repository-relative POSIX path. Must not be absolute and must not escape the repository root.

url.description: Absolute URL, for data held off-repo. Swapping path for url must not require any downstream change.

lfs_oid.description: Git LFS object id, for data tracked by LFS in this repository.

uri.description: Scheme-tagged location for bytes held by a service that is neither this repository nor a plain web server. The SCHEME selects a resolver, so a second host arrives by registering a resolver rather than by minting a schema version. `http` and `https` are deliberately excluded: those are `url`, and one address expressible in two fields is the ambiguity the exactly-one rule exists to prevent. An authority with no dot in it is a deployment ALIAS resolved at fetch time, which is what lets a locator committed to git survive a host migration. The checksum still proves the bytes, so a consumer with no resolver for the scheme fails loudly rather than reading something else.

size_bytes.description: Size in bytes. Checked alongside the checksum, and used by the artifact store to decide whether a transfer is worth making.

format.description: CSV for tabular data, Zarr for bulk arrays, JSON for metadata. Anything else is an instrument-native file that has not been converted yet, and must be layer raw.

media_type.description: IANA media type, for consumers that dispatch on it. Advisory; format is the authoritative field.

compression.description: Compression applied to the stored bytes. The checksum is over the STORED bytes, not the decompressed ones, so recompressing a file changes its manifest entry.

rows.description: For csv: row count excluding header. A cheap equivalence check (TRACE-AI A2).

notes.description: Anything a reader needs in order to use this file that the structured fields do not carry.

$comment: EXACTLY one location, and `oneOf` says both halves at once: zero matches is an entry pointing at nothing, two matches is an entry whose authoritative location a consumer cannot know. The previous form (anyOf plus one `not` per pair) needed three not-clauses for three forms and would need six for four, ten for five -- quadratic in the number of location forms, which is the thing this field exists to stop being expensive. The cost is oneOf's poor error text, and `validate.py::_manifest_location_problem` already pays it for this rule: it is the message a reader actually sees.
